name: Nu Metal
about: Nu metal came out of Southern California in the mid-1990s, when Korn fused downtuned seven-string riffs, hip-hop rhythm, funk bass and Jonathan Davis's confessional, tormented vocals into something neither metal nor rap. Its precursors were Faith No More, Rage Against the Machine and Sepultura's Roots; its sound was mid-tempo, groove-heavy, built on texture and dynamics rather than solos, often with a DJ and a bellowing-to-whispering singer at the center. Between 1998 and 2003 it was the biggest thing in rock: Limp Bizkit, Slipknot, Linkin Park and System of a Down sold tens of millions, while Deftones made its one undisputed art record. A critical backlash and the garage-rock revival ended its run, but its influence returned in the late 2010s through younger bands who grew up on it.

albums.title: Korn
albums.why: Blind's drum-and-bass intro announced a new genre: seven-string sludge, hip-hop bounce and Jonathan Davis's childhood trauma turned into music.

albums.title: White Pony
albums.why: Sacramento's outliers folded shoegaze, trip-hop and Chino Moreno's whispered menace into the one nu-metal album critics outside the genre revere.

albums.title: Toxicity
albums.why: Chop Suey!, Aerials and Serj Tankian's vaudeville-meets-Armenian-folk delivery on the record that proved nu metal could be political, funny and strange.

albums.title: Around the Fur
albums.why: Terry Date's production gave the band's second album a shimmering, bruised atmosphere, with My Own Summer and Be Quiet and Drive its anthems.

albums.title: Rage Against the Machine
albums.why: Tom Morello's turntable-imitating guitar and Zack de la Rocha's agitprop invented the rap-metal template that nu metal borrowed wholesale.

albums.title: Slipknot
albums.why: Ross Robinson's production captured nine Iowans at full fury, with Wait and Bleed and Spit It Out making chaos commercially viable.

albums.title: Iowa
albums.why: Faster, uglier and more death-metal-adjacent than the debut, Iowa is the genre's most extreme number-one album in Britain.

albums.title: Hybrid Theory
albums.why: Chester Bennington's scream, Mike Shinoda's raps and electronics in impeccably produced three-minute songs, and the best-selling rock debut of its decade.

albums.title: Roots
albums.why: Ross Robinson, downtuned guitars and Brazilian percussion on the record that connected groove metal to the nu-metal generation it anticipated.

albums.title: Follow the Leader
albums.why: Freak on a Leash and Got the Life took the band to number one, with Ice Cube and Fred Durst cameos marking the moment the genre went mainstream.

albums.title: System of a Down
albums.why: Sugar and Suite-Pee introduced the band's manic, Zappa-influenced take on the Korn template, rawer and faster than anything to follow.

albums.title: L.D. 50
albums.why: Ryan Martinie's slapped, fretboard-roaming bass and Dig's riff made this the most technically accomplished album of the nu-metal boom.

albums.title: Meteora
albums.why: Numb, Faint and Somewhere I Belong refined the Hybrid Theory formula with sharper hooks, and sold almost as well.

albums.title: Coal Chamber
albums.why: Dez Fafara's barked, goth-flecked debut, with Loco and Sway, is the Roadrunner-era sound before the money arrived.

albums.title: S.C.I.E.N.C.E.
albums.why: Funk, turntables and Brandon Boyd's limber voice on the Calabasas band's second album, before they drifted to alternative rock.

albums.title: Get Some
albums.why: Lynn Strait's punk-funk band made one album before his death in 1998, and it remains a cult favorite among nu metal's first wave.

albums.title: Significant Other
albums.why: Nookie, Break Stuff and the Woodstock '99 fallout: the frat-rap peak of the genre, more skilled than its reputation suggests thanks to Wes Borland.

albums.title: Wisconsin Death Trip
albums.why: Wayne Static's self-described evil disco married industrial sequencing to nu-metal bounce, with Push It its enduring single.

albums.title: Spit
albums.why: Four teenage women from Ontario out-heavied most of their male peers on a debut whose Brackish still turns up on best-of lists.

albums.title: Infest
albums.why: Last Resort was inescapable, and the album around it is leaner and more tuneful than most nu-metal debuts from the Sacramento suburbs.

albums.title: The Sickness
albums.why: David Draiman's staccato vocal tics on Down with the Sickness made the Chicago band a radio institution for two decades.

albums.title: Satellite
albums.why: Released on September 11, 2001, the San Diego Christians' reggae-tinged rap metal gave the year Alive and Youth of the Nation.

albums.title: Fallen
albums.why: Amy Lee's gothic contralto on Bring Me to Life and My Immortal carried nu metal's last multiplatinum debut into pop territory.

albums.title: I Let It In and It Took Everything
albums.why: Liverpool's Loathe mixed Deftones-style shoegaze with djent and nu-metal bounce on the revival's most acclaimed record.
